segments.text: Good day, Mrs. Nováková. Come in.
What do you want to start with today?
Good day. I don't know. I feel like someone pulled my blanket under my leg.
What happened?
After 15 years of marriage, Radka and I decided to divorce.
And I still can't understand it.
Tell me more.
We were still in Croatia. Everything looked normal.
And in September he told me that it's not possible anymore.
How did you manage it?
I was sitting in the kitchen and couldn't say anything.
Then I went to clean the dishes as if nothing was happening.
And what was inside you?
Empty. Then anger. Then again emptiness.
30 times a day.
Radek explained it to you. Why?
He said we pretended to live next to each other.
I didn't notice it or I didn't want to notice it.
What do you think about it now?
That I should have seen it, that I'm blind.
I keep looking back in my head where I made a mistake.
And your own?
No.
Sometimes I think I was too tired and I didn't care about her.
Sometimes I thought I was too much worried.
It seems you are suffering in that hour.
Yes, mainly because of the kids.
Tell me about them.
I have two kids. Anička is 12 and Matěj is 8 years old.
And I don't know how to tell them.
You haven't told them yet?
No. Radek wants us to tell them together.
we keep postponing it.
Anička is already thinking about something.
What did she tell you?
Last week she asked me if we were arguing with dad.
I said no.
I felt terrible.
Why terrible?
Because I lied to her.
And she knew it.
She saw it in my eyes.
What did you think about her?
That I destroy her life.
That I take her home.
How did you manage to tell her the truth?
I would rather have it behind me.
But I'm afraid of their tears.
And Matěj is still a kid, he doesn't understand much.
What would you like to give him?
That we both like him and that it doesn't change.
But I don't know if it's true,
when I don't know how it will look like.
How will it look with the accommodation?
The apartment is on the mortgage.
Radek is getting married to his brother, at least so far.
The children will stay with me.
How do you feel about that?
I'm afraid I won't be able to do it myself.
Radek has always been dealing with money.
What do you do every day?
I work as a Czech teacher at a primary school in Brno.
I teach 9th and 8th graders.
How do you study now?
I go to class with a crutch in my neck.
I feel like everyone sees that my life is falling apart.
Does she know about it somewhere in school?
Only the teacher.
I told her that because I once cried at the walk.
She was nice.
What helped you?
She let me leave earlier, gave me a free hour, but then I was sitting at home and it was worse.
Worse? Why?
Because I was alone at work, I had to do something.
How do you sleep?
Badly. Every night I wake up at 3 a.m. and think about what's next.
What do you say when you wake up?
I don't have a mortgage, I don't have a husband, I don't have anything.
I count the money and imagine how I will tell my children.
It's all over the place.
And then?
I sleep around 5 am and get up at 7.30 am.
I'm tired already in the morning.
Do you eat? Do you move?
I don't eat much. I lost 4 kilos.
My friend tells me that I look terrible.
Do you have anyone you can talk to?
I have a sister in Olomouc, she calls me almost every evening and my friend Eva from work.
What does she say?
She wants almost everything.
Eva just wants me to have a hard time.
She doesn't want me to think about anything.
What are you afraid of?
That I lied.
That a woman who can't keep a marriage is not a good example for children.
That's a hard thought.
Where does it come from?
Probably from my mum. She always said that marriage is a thing and that it's what it is.
What did she say when you introduced her?
She was silent.
Then she said that she hopes I've been good to her.
She hasn't called me much since then.
How do you feel?
Sad.
I need you to forgive me.
What would you like to say?
That it hurts, that I don't want to be alone, but that it doesn't happen here.
What happens when you say it out loud?
I cry and I apologize.
It's nothing. Take your time.
Thank you. I haven't told anyone yet.
What are you doing here?
It's strange to sit here and say it out loud, but it helps a little.
What could help you the most?
Sleep. And you, grandpa, how to say it to your children?
Let's go step by step.
What about sleeping? Have you tried anything?
Cucumber tea and that's all. Doctor offered me some powder, but I don't want to.
Why don't you want to?
I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to wake up for my children in time and I don't want to be dependent.
I see.
Would you try to sit next to the bed, write down what wakes you up?
I could. At least I'll get it out of my head.
And children? What are you most afraid of?
That I'll panic and cry. That I won't be able to stay calm.
So it wouldn't matter?
That I'd be scared of children? That it would be scary for them?
Or they could see that the sadness is allowed.
I didn't think so.
And Ančka is sensitive. Maybe it would help her.
We can see how to prepare it next time.
What are you going to do today?
That I'm not alone and I don't have to manage it right away.
Exactly.
That's all for today.
Thank you. See you next week.
